claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child. My son Alex is 17 and I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he at school, college, doing A-levels, or in approved training?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He actually just left school recently. He's signed up with the careers service to get some help figuring out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know that Alex has registered with the careers service.

**How long ago did Alex leave education?** (I need to know if it's been less than 20 weeks since he left school/education.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been less than 20 weeks - just a few months ago really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. And finally:

**Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning either you live with him, or you're contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Since Alex is 17, has left education recently (less than 20 weeks ago), and has registered with the careers service, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he left education. This special provision is designed to support families during the transition period when young people are deciding their next steps.

You meet all the requirements:
- Alex is under 20 years old
- He left education less than 20 weeks ago
- He has registered with a government-sponsored careers service
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you, so you're responsible for him

Please note that this 20-week period is temporary. After the 20 weeks expire, you would no longer be eligible for Child Benefit unless Alex returns to approved education or training, or starts an apprenticeship that qualifies.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility?

The claimant lives in the UK, Alex lives at home with the claimant (so the claimant is responsible for him), and no one else is claiming for Alex. Therefore, the claimant is eligible for Child Benefit for Alex during this 20-week period.
